subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these six AI-safety event families, field semantics, versioning rules, and trusted/plugin emission boundaries as a permanent core and Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: Merging fixes security-significant provenance semantics and a new public compatibility surface; tests cannot determine whether this taxonomy and ownership model are the intended long-term product contract.

options.title: Approve with boundary repairs
options.body: Sponsor the core taxonomy, but require the public-emitter isolation, per-event schema version, documentation, and exact-path proof before merge.

options.title: Keep semantics plugin-owned
options.body: Reject the dedicated public core taxonomy and expose only a narrower generic diagnostic capability for external safety plugins.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Hold or close the stacked PRs until maintainers define a different observability and trust model.

recommendation.title: Approve with boundary repairs
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core taxonomy, but require the public-emitter isolation, per-event schema version, documentation, and exact-path proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core diagnostics and the public Plugin SDK, making the recent core/plugin API direction owner the best available decision route.
